post.title: 5% down vs 20% down on a $429,100 home: the real math
post.ig:
5% down needs $64,365 less cash than 20% on the August 2026 median home.

NAR's median existing-home price in August 2026: $429,100. Freddie Mac's 30-year rate on Oct 1, 2026: 7.28%.
Example: 20% down = $85,820 and $2,349/month; 5% down = $21,455 and $2,789/month, plus PMI of about $122-$285/month (Freddie Mac's $30-$70 per $100K).
Over 30 years, 5% down pays $94,177 more interest. PMI ends automatically at a scheduled 78% loan-to-value (Homeowners Protection Act).
First-time buyers' median down payment: 10% in NAR's 2025 profile.

Sources: NAR (Sept 2026, 2025 Profile); Freddie Mac PMMS (Oct 1, 2026); CFPB.
